summary: Equinor is still cleaning up after a real cyberattack on its office computers. Gas production is not affected. The NSA's internal network is still being fixed, and reports differ on whether it is back. Officials say the recent outages are separate and report no coordinated attack.

events.title: Equinor still cleaning up after cyberattack on IT systems
events.impact: Equinor says production is not affected and it sees no sign of stolen data. An employee said internal email was down. There is no time estimate for full recovery.
events.stated_cause: Equinor calls it a cyberattack but not a virus, so it says it will not spread. On Nov 18 it said it better understands how it happened. Nobody has named who did it.

events.title: NSA classified internal network still being restored; reports differ
events.impact: On Nov 18 a senior official told CNN that patching is going slower than expected. Core national security work is said to be unaffected. An earlier CBS report said the network was running again.
events.stated_cause: The Director of National Intelligence linked it to urgent patching of PHP software flaws. The NSA first said routine maintenance. No official source reports a cyber attack.

events.title: Officials say no sign recent outages are linked or caused by attackers
events.impact: US officials call the outages separate technical problems. Some experts and the public still question the timing. This is an official view, not a proven finding.
events.stated_cause: Officials point to patching, router work and software bugs. They name no attacker.

events.title: US stocks fall Tue and Wed; futures up Thursday
events.impact: Tue: Dow fell 848 points to 50,759. Wed: Dow fell 561 to 50,198, S&P 500 fell 0.2% to 7,324, Nasdaq rose 0.4% to 24,430. Futures are higher Thursday. I saw no trading halts.
events.stated_cause: Reports point to Nvidia earnings, AI stock worries and Fed rate-hike fears. No technical or attack cause reported.

events.title: Bitcoin about 62.7K to 64.2K USD, down roughly 14% on the week
events.impact: Fortune shows 63,748 at 6am ET. CoinGecko shows about 63,469 and CoinMarketCap about 64,186. It is a slow slide, not a crash. I found no exchange outage.
events.stated_cause: CoinGecko cites Fed rate-hike fears and fund outflows. No technical or attack cause reported.

events.title: Malware reportedly spread to 178 websites through a web vendor
events.impact: One local TV report says a third-party web vendor, Optimizely, was used to spread malware that steals card data. It names big sites as customers. I found no wire or agency confirmation.
events.stated_cause: A cyberattack through a third-party vendor, per one local TV report. Not verified by a second source.

events.title: Ransomware gang claims Visa and JPMorgan; both dispute impact
events.impact: A gang called n0n set a 48-hour leak deadline. Visa says a third-party provider in Asia Pacific was hit, not its own systems. Chase says its outage was a software bug.
events.stated_cause: The gang's claim is unverified. Visa blames a third-party provider. Chase says it has no evidence of a cyberattack.

events.title: FAA nationwide ground stop; Juniper router installs paused
events.impact: Flights have resumed. The FAA feed at 12:52 UTC shows only a weather delay at Orlando. The FAA paused new Juniper router installs.
events.stated_cause: The FAA says a new router flooded the network with data. Officials say routine telecom maintenance set it off. The FBI is helping to rule out an attack.

events.title: Chase banking services disrupted
events.impact: Some Chase customers could not use certain services on Monday. Chase looks operational now.
events.stated_cause: Chase says a software bug in an on-site hardware system caused it. It says it has no evidence of a cyberattack.

events.title: Apple services (iCloud, App Store) outage
events.impact: Apple Music, the App Store and AppleCare were briefly disrupted. Apple says services are back up.
events.stated_cause: Apple says an internal update caused it. It told media it was not a cyberattack.

events.title: Cloudflare status page shows degraded performance
events.impact: The status page lists degraded performance for Sites and Services, last changed 08:56 UTC today. I saw no wire report of a wide outage.
events.stated_cause: Unknown. Cloudflare has not given a cause in the data I saw.

events.title: CISA adds four actively exploited flaws to its list
events.impact: Routine notice covering Synology, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap software. I saw no new Emergency Directive. The notice does not mention the outages.
events.stated_cause: Attackers are exploiting software flaws. CISA gives no link to the outages.

connection_assessment.reasoning: The FAA stop is blamed on a router that flooded the network. Chase blames a software bug, Apple an internal update, and the NSA outage is linked to urgent software patching. Equinor reports a real cyberattack, and nobody has named who did it. No official source links these events.
connection_assessment.would_change_my_mind: An official statement blaming the same company or attacker, or several big systems failing at the same moment, would make me think they are connected.

alert.reason: No new confirmed link between events, and no new major outage in the last few hours.

prep_note: No action is needed for most people. Keep a little cash on hand and check flight status before travel. Use strong passwords and install software updates when offered. Ignore posts claiming a scheduled national blackout, because National Grid called that rumor false.
